title: When the saxophone arrived in New Orleans
summary: Barnes says clarinetists like Kaiser did not play saxophone, and the saxophone came to the city late, with Big Eye Louis bringing one back.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well now these fellas, Kaiser and Blind Charlie, did they play sax too or just clarinet?

No, no, they just clarinet. Well I'm telling you saxophone just came out here a couple of years ago, you know. But saxophone was a sign. Well saxophone was an offense when you see what Joe Allen and Sheldon Sten and Mads had sax and Mads from Williams but they had good clarinet players. But they had clarinet and sax. He was like, now you might double up with a sax. Yeah, you might double up.
Well how about in these little tonk bands that you and Bichet and Louis played in, would anybody play sax in those bands?

No, no. When Bichet pushed left from here we knew nothing about sax. I knew who was playing sax. I don't remember. Because Louis went away, big old Louis went away and he came back here with the sax. And he come back here I said he gave the sax away. I just bought it because he couldn't buy it.
